correctness.rationale: Essential computations verified independently. (1) HNF covering: count identity sum_{d1d2d3=20} d1^2*d2 =1085 verified; 18 ordered diagonal types enumerated, per-type counts match d1^2*d2, reversal symmetry sum d2*d3^2=1085 holds; column-convention covering argument (any T=conv{0,w1,w2,w3} with W=[w1w2w3] has left-HNF H=UW in list; translation to origin loses no generality; ordering duplicates harmless) is sound modulo cited Cohen Alg 2.4.5/2.4.8, whose transpose correspondence (H^T upper-triangular row-bounded) was checked to match stated bounds. Both signs covered since product is |det|. (2) Ehrhart inversion h1=L1-4, h2=L2-10-4h1, h3=L3-20-10h1-4h2 derived from L(t)=sum hi*C(t+3-i,3) and checked algebraically; sum hi=det and h3=interior theory correct; L(-1)=-h3 identity makes L(-1)==-interior equivalent to h3==interior, so the two listed checks are redundant not independent, but both hold. (3) Counting: bounding boxes 0<=x<=t*d1, 0<=y<=t*max(a21,d2), 0<=z<=t*max(a31,a32,d3) proved to contain tT; barycentric integer formulas (M2=y*d1-x*a21, M3=z*d1*d2-x*a31*d2-M2*a32, NS=x*d2*d3+M2*d3+M3) and strict-interior variants verified correct; facet determinant half-space test with centroid C=v1+v2+v3 reference signs verified correct. Ran provided verify.py: VERIFY PASS (1085 count, dual agreement on all 1085x3, 24-set identical, max-width 2 with 318 attaining, White cert). Independently re-implemented third counting route (generic Cramer-rule Fractions over generous [-1,max+1] box) on 14 edge/extremal cases plus 60 random (d,t) cases: all match census L/I and confirm no points outside tight boxes. Random affine-coverage test (30 random integer matrices det +-20 with random translations, generic-vertex counting): all h* land in logged 39-set, supporting completeness. (4) Width: y=(M^T)u bound |y|_inf<=w-1 => |u|_inf<=rmax*(w-1) with rmax=max row-sum of (M^T)^{-1} (explicit Fractions n11=1/d1, n12=-a21/d1d2, n23=-a32/d2d3, n13=(a21a32-a31d2)/d1d2d3) is sound; width>=1 for nonzero u (integer dots, full-dimensional) certifies w*=1. Brute-forced all 597 h01 widths over primitive directions to bound 6 and recomputed exact Bcert: max is 2, attaining 318, matching claim; outside-stratum width-3 example H=(4,0,5,2,4,1) wit (-1,-1,1) verified width 3. Per-rep widths/witnesses/Bcert in witnesses.json all re-verified. White empty cert: U=[[0,1,0],[0,0,1],[1,0,0]] det 1 maps {(20,1,1),(0,1,0),(0,0,1)} to {(1,1,20),(1,0,0),(0,1,0)}=White T(1,1,20), verified; empty HNF count 21 all share h*=(1,0,19,0) with L=(4,29,96), consistent with theory that empty => h1=0. Hibi h1>=h3 and L(-1)==-interior hold for all 1085. Two non-essential presentation slips noted but not fatal: draft says max box at t=3 has <=976 points, actual max is 205204 points for H=(20,19,1,19,0,1) (976 is the empty-rep box 61*4*4); draft says Bcert<=1 throughout h01 stratum (<=27 dirs), actual max rmax over h01 is 8/5 with 20/597 cases needing Bcert=2 (<=125 dirs) — verifier correctly uses per-tetra Bcert so max-2 conclusion remains certified, just with larger tiny box for those 20. These are fixable text errors, not failures of the 24-set census.

originality.rationale: No prior result substantively covers the joint hollow+once-punctured V=20 h* 24-set. Compared substantively: (a) White empty-tetrahedra theorem (exposition arXiv:1610.01981) is parametric infinite family T(a,b,q) for empty (L1=4) only; it implies the single empty h* (1,0,19,0) with L1=4=>h=(1,0,V-1,0) but gives no compiled list for the 15 hollow-with-boundary vectors (L1>4) nor 8 once-punctured vectors, and no (L1,L2,L3) certificates or width maxima at fixed V. Draft correctly uses White only as consistency for one case. (b) Lattice 3-polytopes with few points (Blanco-Santos arXiv:1409.6701, 5-point infinite width-1 families +9 width-2 classes and 6-point 74+2 classes) is organized by total point count <=6; V=20 h01 tetrahedra carry L1=4..23 points (up to 23 boundary points, e.g. (1,19,0,0) L=23), overwhelmingly outside <=6 range; even the 5-6 point overlap (e.g. (1,1,18,0) L1=5) is not compiled as a volume-stratified h* table there. (c) Width-1 multi-width classification (arXiv:2304.03627) gives parametric (w1,w2,w3) families and counting functions, not a fixed-volume complete h* list with Ehrhart certificates and extremal width witness. (d) GRDB index (grdb.co.uk) holds Fano/reflexive/canonical tables, not a per-volume hollow+once-punctured tetrahedron h* stratum; no such V=20 table listed. Normaliz docs confirm capability, not precompiled table. Direct webfetch of the three arXiv URLs failed with transport/SSL errors (offline), so comparison rests on titles/comparisons supplied in topic.json plus standard knowledge, but substantive disjointness in object (fixed-volume h* set vs parametric families/point-count/reflexive tables), method (exhaustive HNF-plus-dual-count certificates vs structural classification), and claim type (exact 24-set membership+non-membership vs infinite families) is clear. A timestamp or failed search was not used to establish priority. Narrowly new: no validated SCOPE finding or failed attempt covers HNF Ehrhart census at V=20. Hence originality passes, though value fails separately.

value.rationale: Even though correct and narrowly new, the result as stated is not independently worth finding later: it is a mere parameter substitution and unexplained single-volume enumeration. Decisive evidence: (1) Same textbook HNF-plus-brute-force pipeline yields analogous censuses at neighboring divisor-rich volumes with no new ideas — auditor recomputed V=12 (455 HNF -> 17 total, 13 h01: 10 hollow+3 once-punctured) and V=18 (910 HNF -> 29 total, 20 h01) in seconds using identical code, and V=30 has 2821 HNF. V=20 (1085 HNF -> 39 total, 24 h01) is one arbitrary instance among infinite volumes; choosing 20 has no principled threshold. Draft's 'smallest divisor-rich volume beyond textbook examples where all diagonal types interact' is factually false: V=12=2^2*3 has identical divisor structure (6 divisors, 18 ordered diagonal types) and is smaller, also has both i=0 and i=1 strata populated and L1 up to 15 (beyond 6-point Blanco-Santos range). Richness merely grows with V. (2) Claimed extremal witnesses are trivial or single-volume computations without general insight: max-h1=19 is immediate from sum hi=V, h0=1, hi>=0 => h1<=V-1, attained by obvious infinite long-edge family conv{0,(1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,V)} giving h*=(1,V-1,0,0) for any V — no search needed. Max-width 2 over h01 at V=20 is a finite check (318/597 attain) with no theorem explaining pattern, and gaps (hollow missing h1=8,16,17,18 / L1=12,20,21,22; once-punctured missing h1=0,2) are logged without explanation. Certificates (HNF reps, L-triples, reciprocity, Hibi h1>=h3) verify correctness but do not explain why those 24 occur. Width-3-outside example shows non-triviality of the bound at this V only, not a structural result. (3) Motivation (toric-code/Fano benchmarks, reusable pipeline) is generic: no recognized open problem asks for V=20 specifically; GRDB/Fano interest is in reflexive/canonical families, not a single hollow-inclusive volume slice; pipeline is standard HNF generation + tiny-box enumeration (stdlib, <2min), not a new scalable method. Citability as anchor table is low since any CAS can recompute in ~1min and the next volume would need a new table. This matches SCOPE value-reject precedents for fixed-parameter exhaustive enumerations (e.g. RT(30,K4,6), SmallGroup(96) extrema) even when correct and certified. Therefore fails the 'independently worth finding later' bar; it is an unexplained enumeration / parameter instance, not a substantive closure.
